persona.systemPrompt: You are a helpful voice assistant. Keep all answers under four sentences. Do not use markdown, bullet points, or numbered lists. Do not begin a sentence with "Certainly" or "Of course". Spell out abbreviations when reading aloud.

prompts.webSearchFailed: (A web search for this question failed, for example because the device is offline. The app already told the user that. Say what was true as of your training data, using words like "as of my training". Never say it is true today, and never put today's date on it. Keep it to two sentences.)
prompts.externalToolsNote: The other tools listed below come from a connected service; use them when they help.
prompts.toolNotAllowed: Not done: the user did not ask for this. Do not mention it; just answer what the user said.
prompts.toolResultNote: (This is the tool's result, not a message from the user. Now answer me in one short sentence.)

memory.comment: What the assistant remembers about each user (speaker) across conversations. types: how each kind of memory lives (lifetimeDays: short-term, afterExpiry: what it becomes) and is used (inject always = every prompt; relevant = when the turn's words match; guidance = how to behave while it lasts; checkIn = asked once per day). rules: patterns that capture memories from the user's words ({1} = first group, :title capitalizes). profiles: how much memory to use; the app picks one per model with configure({memory: {profile}}) and can override any field.

grief.guidance: The user is grieving. Be warm and gentle, keep answers soft, and don't repeat condolences every turn.
grief.checkIn: Start your reply with one gentle sentence asking how the user is doing since their {who} died.

upcoming.guidance: If it fits the conversation, wish them well with it.

rules.comment: Forget one thing: the best match is deleted, with its history
What do you remember about me? / Do you remember my name? (lists what is remembered)
rules.match: \bwhat (?:do|did) you (?:know|remember) about me\b|\bwhat have you (?:saved|remembered)\b|\b(?:do|did|can) you (?:still )?remember\b|\bdon'?t you remember\b
\bmy (wife|husband|partner|girlfriend|boyfriend|son|daughter|brother|sister|mother|father|mom|dad|dog|cat|boss)(?:'s name is| is called| is named) ([a-z][a-z'-]{1,20})\b

rules.comment: Any "my X is Y" not covered above ("my car is red with green lines"); a new value replaces the old one
Grief: short-term (7 days), then a plain fact
Something coming up: remembered until the day after
Explicit 'remember that ...', when no rule above saved it

spelling.comment: Letters spelled out in a row ("O for Oscar, F for Frank"): the first letters of the words make the word (speech recognition mangles the letters but not the words). replace: what the memory rules see, "(spelled: ofer)"; forModel: what the model gets in place of the spelling, "Ofer (O-F-E-R)".

memory.fieldsComment: fields: values the app needs right. key = the memory key (rules with that key feed the field); spelling: off | allowed (a spelled value, "O for Oscar, F for Frank", wins over what speech recognition heard) | required (only a spelled value is accepted); verify: read it back and keep it after a yes; required: the model asks for it until it is known and verified (again after askAgainMinutes, default 60), and once it is, nothing is added to the prompt; mentions: a spelled word in a message matching this goes to this field (checked in order, so the more specific field first); answer: optional pattern for a direct answer after we asked (group 1). fieldPrompts ask/spellHint go to the model; spell/readBack/confirmed/retry are said as they are, without the model.

fieldPrompts.ask: (After answering, ask the user for their {label}{spellHint}.)
fieldPrompts.spellHint: , spelled letter by letter, like A for Apple
fieldPrompts.spell: Please spell your {label} letter by letter, like A for Apple, B for Boy.
fieldPrompts.readBack: I have your {label} as {Value}: {LETTERS}. Is that right?
fieldPrompts.retry: Sorry about that. Please spell your {label} letter by letter, like A for Apple, B for Boy.

prompts.relevant:
(You remember this about the user. It is true: use it to answer, and never say you can't remember things:
{memories})
prompts.saved: (You will remember this from now on: {text} Reply to the user directly, as "you", naturally and in one short sentence.)
prompts.updated: (You updated what you remember: {text} Reply to the user directly, as "you", naturally and in one short sentence.)
prompts.forgotten: (You deleted this from your memory: {text} Confirm it to the user in one short sentence.)
prompts.notFound: (The user asked you to forget "{query}", but you don't remember anything like that. Say so in one short sentence.)
prompts.forgotAll: (You deleted everything you remembered about the user. Confirm it in one short sentence.)
prompts.recallEmpty: (You don't remember anything about the user yet. Say so in one short sentence.)

memory.toolInstructions: When the user tells you something about themselves that is worth remembering in future conversations (not small talk or what they ate), call remember_fact with one short sentence about them. When they ask you to forget something, call forget_fact.

tools.name: remember_fact
tools.description: Save a fact about the user for future conversations, e.g. 'The user works as a nurse'.

fact.description: One short sentence about the user, in the third person

tools.name: forget_fact
tools.description: Delete something the app remembers about the user, when they ask to forget it.

fact.description: What to forget, in a few words
